judge.review: Independent read-only review, 2026-10-01; did not author these files

rulings:
REJECTED. Exhaustive one-round review of original steps 0 through 62, including credentials, temporal state, captured paths, request content, demanded calls and refusals.
L1. Steps 2,3: delete both uncaused authentication refusals (the same cause twice consecutively). Record any resulting defensive-branch coverage with a vendor-backed reason rather than contriving a replacement refusal.
L2. Steps 14,15,16: in 14 capture the form action from the hosted page (the runner supports text:<regex>). In 15 submit that captured action instead of constructing co_url + /pay, and rename the action as supplying payment details and starting a free trial with no immediate charge. Delete 16: a failing repeat of the completed request in this sitting is expressly rejected by the bar; a 'lost response' written only in its title does not override that rule.
L3. Steps 19,20,21,23: after 19 add a two-hour wait to let the newly created World run. In 20 report completed hour IDs for 2026-01-14T15 and 2026-01-14T16, not T10/T11 preceding creation at 15:00. In 21 retry the actual T16 event. Reduce 23's wait from 27030m to 26910m so it still reaches 2 February 09:30.
L4. Step 26: delete the disconnected duplicate-email customer creation (no Labs billing/portal request causes it). Keep 28–30, whose refusal has a concrete missing-customer cause and subsequent support intervention.
L5. Steps 35,36,37,39,40,47,48,49,51: after 35 GET its captured pco_url and capture its displayed Pay form action before Grace leaves the tab. Set 36's wait to 1500m (25 hours), reflecting the vendor's 24-hour TTL. Submit the captured stale form action in 37. In 39 GET pco_url returned by 38 rather than rebuilding buy.polar.sh from the secret; capture its new form action and submit it in 40. Set 47 to Thursday 12 February with wait 1380m (23 hours after Grace returns at Wednesday 11 February 10:30). After 48 GET its returned mco_url and capture the displayed form action; submit it in 49. Set 51's wait to 90720m to retain Thursday 16 April 09:30. The new page-read after 35 and after 48 belong to those original step numbers for apply-rulings. Fix the twin TTL along with the life, using Polar's published config/model source; never hide the twin's 1-hour expiry defect in expectations.
L6. Step 46: delete the fabricated unknown-checkout refusal; no actor has caused this request beyond the author choosing a fake id.
L7. Steps 60,62: delete the filtered email/name read-backs after this same refresh actor already retrieved the complete collections in 59/61. Preserve the full refresh lists 56–59,61.
All remaining original steps passed the bar. Vendor sources: polar/spec/openapi.json.gz CheckoutProductsCreate and CheckoutConfirmStripe; https://polar.sh/docs/features/checkout/session; https://polar.sh/docs/features/subscriptions/trials; https://github.com/polarsource/polar/blob/main/server/polar/config.py CHECKOUT_TTL_SECONDS = 24 hours; model checkout.py uses that value. Dates were independently calculated from 2026-01-01 and all waits. Demand verified from cached twin-world 96ca4478bb39 and open-autonomy 0841076bed91.
doubts: The customer-life frame calls this a year although it ends in April, and the full life does not show leaving the vendor; this is a scope/wording doubt rather than a ruling under the explicit rejection list.
